title: Bayes' Theorem in the Doctor's Office
tagline: A positive test for a rare disease usually means you are still healthy.

chapters.title: Start with the actual number of sick people
chapters.summary: In 100,000 people only 100 actually have the disease.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: If only one person in a thousand has this disease, how many blue squares should I picture in a crowd of one hundred thousand?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Exactly one hundred blue squares. The rest, ninety-nine thousand nine hundred, stay gray.

chapters.title: Count the true positives
chapters.summary: Of those 100 diseased people, 99 will test positive.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: So the test catches almost all of them, right?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Ninety-nine of the one hundred blue squares get a bright green outline. Only one blue square stays plain.

chapters.title: Count the false positives
chapters.summary: Of the 99,900 healthy people, 4,995 will still test positive.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Now the healthy people. How many of them get a green outline by mistake?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Five percent of the ninety-nine thousand nine hundred gray squares. That is four thousand nine hundred ninety-five gray squares with green outlines.

chapters.title: Put all the green squares together
chapters.summary: The total number of positive tests is 5,094, most of which come from healthy people.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: If I add the two groups that tested positive, what do I see?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Ninety-nine blue-green squares next to four thousand nine hundred ninety-five gray-green squares. The gray pile is fifty times bigger.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: So most positive tests are actually false alarms.

chapters.title: Find the real chance after a positive test
chapters.summary: Only about 2% of people who test positive actually have the disease.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: If I divide the true positives by every green square, what number do I get?

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Ninety-nine divided by five thousand ninety-four. That is roughly two percent.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: So even after the positive result, the odds I actually have the disease are only two in a hundred.

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Exactly. The base rate of the disease keeps most of those green outlines on healthy people.

takeaways: Count the actual sick and healthy people first before looking at test results.
False positives from the huge healthy group usually outnumber true positives.
A positive test raises your chance only to about two percent when the disease is this rare.
